answer: Newcomers join a small mutual insurance pool, sponsored by existing members who stake their own standing on the recruit. The pool pays victims when a member cheats, so sponsors vet strangers carefully and a farm must infiltrate many independent pools to scale. Like a nebula, pools drift apart — no single controller spans them; like a canyon, the gap between pools cannot be bridged by fakes alone. One fraud drains the farm's own pool and leaves a sable mark on every member, so honesty is cheaper than forgery. Clean pools earn the right to sponsor more recruits, so vetting compounds.
